quickAnswerTitle: Quick Answer: Comfort Colors vs Gildan 5000?
quickAnswer: When evaluating comfort colors vs gildan, choose the Comfort Colors 1717 for premium streetwear, luxury softness, and trendy vintage aesthetics: its 6.1 oz heavyweight ringspun cotton and pre-shrunk garment-dyed wash make it superior. Choose the Gildan 5000 for budget bulk promotions, giveaways, and event merchandise where low per-unit cost and consistent piece-dyed colors are the priority.
intro: When choosing between comfort colors vs gildan for blank t-shirts, custom merchandise, or everyday casual wear, the difference comes down to fabric softness, shrinkage, silhouette, and dyeing methods. While Gildan actually owns Comfort Colors, both labels cater to completely different markets. Comfort Colors focuses on heavyweight, vintage ringspun cotton, while Gildan 5000 delivers reliable, budget-friendly bulk blanks.

sections.heading: 1. Difference Between Gildan and Comfort Colors at a Glance
paragraphs: The primary difference between Gildan and Comfort Colors lies in cotton processing, fabric weight, and dyeing techniques. Comfort Colors 1717 is crafted from 100% combed ringspun cotton weighing 6.1 oz per square yard, yielding a soft, thick handfeel that mimics high-end vintage tees.

The Gildan 5000 uses 5.3 oz carded open-end cotton. It feels lighter and noticeably stiffer out of the shipping box. While Gildan 5000 is the industry king for budget-friendly screen printing runs, Comfort Colors 1717 dominates the premium creator and streetwear merchandise market.

bullets.label: Comfort Colors 1717
bullets.text: 6.1 oz heavyweight ringspun cotton, garment-dyed, pre-shrunk, relaxed boxy cut, vintage muted palette.

bullets.label: Gildan 5000
bullets.text: 5.3 oz midweight carded cotton, piece-dyed, standard tubular fit, ultra-low cost, bright vibrant colors.

sections.heading: 2. Who Owns Comfort Colors? The Gildan Connection Explained
paragraphs: A common question among shoppers and print shops is: who owns Comfort Colors? Comfort Colors was originally founded in 1975 by Barry Chouinard in Vermont. In 2015, Gildan Activewear acquired Comfort Colors for approximately $100 million.

Although Gildan owns Comfort Colors, the manufacturing and dyeing processes remain separate. Gildan preserved Comfort Colors' proprietary garment-dye facility in North Carolina to maintain the authentic washed aesthetic that fans love, while scaling global distribution through Gildan's massive supply chain.

sections.heading: 3. Fabric & Dyeing: Garment Dye vs. Traditional Piece Dye
paragraphs: Dyeing is where the visual contrast between comfort colors vs gildan is most apparent. Comfort Colors 1717 undergoes garment-dyeing, meaning the t-shirt is fully cut, sewn, and washed before being soaked in dye. This creates subtle fading along seams, eliminates factory shrinkage, and produces comfortable, broken-in pastel hues.

Gildan 5000 uses piece-dyeing, where huge bolts of fabric are dyed prior to cutting and sewing. Piece-dyeing produces uniform, highly saturated primary colors that do not fade, but the fabric lacks the tactile character and softness of garment-dyed cotton.

sections.heading: 4. Shrinkage and Washing Durability
paragraphs: Shrinkage is a major factor when ordering blank tees. Because Comfort Colors 1717 shirts are washed and pre-shrunk multiple times during the garment-dyeing process, they experience virtually zero shrinkage (under 1-2%) when machine washed in cold water.
In contrast, the Gildan 5000 is not pre-shrunk. You can expect standard open-end cotton shrinkage of roughly 3% to 5% in total length and chest width after the first warm wash and tumble dry cycle.

sections.heading: 5. Fit, Silhouette & Sizing: Streetwear Boxy vs. Standard Cut
paragraphs: Comfort Colors 1717 features a trendy, slightly boxy drop-shoulder cut with thick 1-inch ribbed collar bands that do not stretch out or bacon-fold over time. It drapes naturally over the torso without clinging.

Gildan 5000 has a classic tubular cut without side seams, fitting more like a traditional utility undershirt. For modern styling, pair a washed pepper or terracotta Comfort Colors tee with relaxed utility trousers or chinos. Explore our guide on [what color shirt goes with olive green pants](/blog/what-color-shirt-goes-with-olive-green-pants) or test earthy color combinations on our [interactive color wheel tool](/color-matcher).

sections.heading: 6. Price vs. Value Comparison
paragraphs: At wholesale volume, a Gildan 5000 blank tee typically costs between $2.50 and $4.00, making it unbeatable for charity runs, corporate giveaways, and budget screen printing. Comfort Colors 1717 blanks cost between $8.00 and $11.50 wholesale, retailing anywhere from $22 to $35 as finished streetwear merch.
If you want maximum profit margin on a promotional giveaway, Gildan wins. If you want customers to wear and love your apparel for years, the Comfort Colors 1717 is well worth the extra investment.

faqs.question: Who owns Comfort Colors?
faqs.answer: Gildan Activewear owns Comfort Colors. Gildan acquired the vintage garment-dyed brand in 2015 for roughly $100 million, while keeping Comfort Colors' unique dyeing methods and premium heavyweight cotton specs separate from standard Gildan products.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Gildan and Comfort Colors?
faqs.answer: The main difference between Gildan and Comfort Colors is cotton quality, weight, and dyeing. Comfort Colors 1717 is a 6.1 oz heavyweight ringspun cotton tee that is pre-shrunk and garment-dyed for a soft, vintage feel. Gildan 5000 is a 5.3 oz carded cotton tee that is piece-dyed for uniform bright color and sold at a budget-friendly price point.

faqs.question: Do Comfort Colors 1717 t-shirts shrink in the wash?
faqs.answer: No. Because Comfort Colors 1717 shirts undergo intense pre-washing during their garment-dyeing process, they experience virtually zero shrinkage (under 1-2%) when washed in cold water and tumbled dry on low.

faqs.question: Is Comfort Colors better quality than standard Gildan?
faqs.answer: Yes. Comfort Colors 1717 uses tightly twisted ringspun cotton yarns and reinforced double-needle stitching, resulting in a noticeably softer handfeel, better drape, and longer lifespan than standard Gildan 5000 carded cotton.

faqs.question: Why is Comfort Colors more expensive than Gildan?
faqs.answer: Comfort Colors costs more because it uses higher-grade ringspun cotton, heavier 6.1 oz fabric weight, and a specialized garment-dyeing wash process that requires extra labor and individualized garment washing.
